answer: Trellis Path Accrual. Each identity's trust score is the sum of signed attestations along a recorded interaction path, anchored to a randomly sampled vertex in the prior graph. Cloning requires reproducing that path history, costing one real interaction per edge plus a yarrow-seeded audit bond that is slashed on failed cross-checks. A clone's expected payoff is below zero because the audit cost exceeds any duplicate benefit.
